articles.title: After failed Maxx Crosby trade, Ravens reportedly had Cam Jurgens take physical before deal with Eagles was finalized
articles.summary: Ravens doctors traveled to Philadelphia on Wednesday morning to give Jurgens the exam before the trade was announced.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens learned from the failed March Maxx Crosby trade as they prepared a deal this week to acquire center Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , in order to speed up the process to finalize the trade, the Ravens and Eagles set up a physical for Jurgens in Philadelphia before consummating the deal. A pair of Ravens doctors traveled to the Eagles' training facility on Wednesday morning and gave Jurgens his physical exam. Once he was found to be fit, the trade was finalized and announced.

The process was different from seven months ago when it was reported that the Ravens were acquiring Crosby, a five-time Pro Bowler, from the Las Vegas Raiders pending a physical.

Four days after the news broke, the Raiders announced that the Ravens had backed out of the trade agreement , which was later reported due to Crosby, who played last season with a left knee injury and needed offseason surgery to repair the meniscus in the knee, failing his physical.

The Jurgens trade, which saw the Ravens send the Eagles a pair of future draft picks in exchange for the 27-year-old and a 2027 seventh-rounder, was not contingent on a physical being passed since the exam had already taken place. Usually players travel to their potential new team in order to be checked out before a trade is made official.

After the Crosby deal fell through, the Ravens pivoted and signed Trey Hendrickson to a four-year, $112 million contract in free agency.

Jurgens will not make his debut this week for the Ravens as he remains in concussion protocol. He is expected to be available for Baltimore's Week 6 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

articles.title: Prediction markets' NFL boom tests sports betting rules
articles.summary: Prediction markets built their business by letting users trade on everything from Federal Reserve decisions to pop culture. This year's football season is sh...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Prediction markets built their business by letting users trade on everything from Federal Reserve decisions to pop culture. This year's football season is showing just how much their growth hinges on something more familiar to bettors: sports.

Last weekend, games in the National Football League and the NCAA boosted trading volumes at Kalshi Inc. and Polymarket to consecutive daily records for a two-day total of $8.56 billion, according to data compiled by Dune Analytics. The combined weekly volume for both companies reached a record $22.2 billion.

Their new mainstream popularity puts prediction markets on a collision course with traditional sportsbooks, state regulators and the NFL, which has raised concerns about the effect of the trades on game integrity. The tensions are raising the stakes for the industry, just as a potential Supreme Court showdown may threaten its business model.

In the first four weeks of the NFL season, the financial impact for the top platforms has surged into view: More than 80% of Kalshi's volume came from sports trades in September. The company is considering a potential initial public offering after a financing round valued the platform at about $40 billion.

"It's the same playbook we saw five years ago with online betting apps," said Jordan Bender, an analyst at Citizens Financial Group. "It looks no different."

Those betting companies are pushing back as they face a regulatory disadvantage: Prediction markets are federally classified as exchanges, meaning they can avoid state taxes on traditional gambling — like New York's 51% levy — as well as age and location restrictions on sportsbooks.

That's pushing betting sites such as DraftKings Inc. and FanDuel to launch their own prediction-market products, giving them access to customers in states where their sportsbooks can't operate. For now, they're trailing Kalshi and Polymarket in trading volume and customer adoption.

"In Texas or California, where gambling is not allowed, prediction markets have a leg up," said Ilya Beylin, an associate law professor at Seton Hall University.

Kalshi says its products shouldn't be considered gambling because it operates as an exchange and doesn't take the other side of customers' trades. "Sports trading on regulated prediction markets offer a fairer choice to consumers, with no 'house' that restricts winners and hooks people the more they lose," said Elisabeth Diana, Kalshi's head of communications.

articles.title: Jeremiah Trotter Jr., Bryan Thomas Jr. Ejected After Massive Fight to Start Eagles-Jags in London
articles.summary: It didn't take long for chaos to break out in Sunday's London game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
It didn't take long for chaos to break out in Sunday's London game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles.

Jacksonville's Josh Cameron returned the opening kickoff for a touchdown only for it to be called back for holding. However, that was just the start of things, as a fight broke out after the play that resulted in the ejection of Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr.

Notably, the ejection for Jacksonville was not for the wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.

In terms of the overall importance of each player, this was more of a blow for Philadelphia.

Trotter has established himself as an important part of the NFC East team's linebacker rotation in his third season since entering the league as a 2024 fifth-round draft pick. Through the first four games, he tallied 19 tackles and a pass defended.

Considering his career-high for tackles is 32 from last year, the Clemson product seems well on his way to his best season.

It was also another loss for an Eagles team playing without Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Jonathan Greenard, among others.

As for Jacksonville, Thomas posted just one tackle and 0.5 sacks through his first three appearances this season. While he sees playing time on special teams and in the defensive rotation, he isn't one of the team's most important players.

Look for the Jaguars to continue relying on Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen to continue leading the pass-rush against the Eagles. They also don't have to worry about Barkley in the backfield, which will allow them to key on Jalen Hurts throughout the game.

articles.title: Bryan Thomas Jr. and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. ejected for fighting during kickoff in London
articles.summary: Bryan Thomas Jr. and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. got ejected on a play that didn't even count.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. and Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. didn't last long in Week 5. Both players were ejected after the opening kickoff after getting into a physical altercation at midfield on Sunday.

The kickoff was initially returned for a touchdown, but offsetting penalties resulted in the kick having to be replayed.

After the return, however, a fight broke out between Thomas and Trotter, though the broadcast missed the actual altercation.

After a commercial break, the broadcast showed a portion of the play. After the Jaguars' return man broke free, Thomas and Trotter were spotted blocking each other down the field. After engaging with each other for some time, Trotter eventually threw Thomas to the ground. The broadcast missed the rest of the fight.

The play, which initially looked like a touchdown, was called back due to offsetting penalties. The Eagles lined up illegally and the Jaguars were called for holding. Because of that, the opening kickoff needed to be replayed.

In addition to that, both Thomas and Trotter were called for their own offsetting penalties, which caused both players to be ejected.

Notably, it was Jacksonville linebacker Bryan Thomas Jr. who was ejected from the contest. Receiver Brian Thomas Jr. was not involved in the play.

articles.title: Mike Ditka Honored by Bears with Helmet Patch After Death
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears will honor legendary coach Mike Ditka during Sunday's game against the rival Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears will honor legendary coach Mike Ditka during Sunday's game against the rival Green Bay Packers.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport shared a look at the helmet decals Chicago will wear with Ditka's No. 89:

Ditka died at the age of 86, and his family released a statement on Friday through Jarrett Payton , the son of iconic Bears running back Walter Payton.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka," the statement said. "While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears' Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever."

It is impossible to tell the story of the Bears without a significant focus on Ditka's impact.

He started his playing career in the Windy City and was a Pro Bowler in each of his first five seasons. He won a NFL championship in his third season after he set an NFL rookie tight end record with 1,076 receiving yards.

That mark stood until Brock Bowers surpassed it in 2024.

Ditka's 12 touchdown catches that season still stands as a rookie tight end record.

While Ditka continued his playing career with the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys, he returned to the Bears as their head coach from 1982 through 1992. Chicago won the Super Bowl during the 1985 season and reached the playoffs in seven of his 10 years as the head coach.

Following his death, the Bears honored Ditka with a video montage and a statement:

"Mike's impact on the Chicago Bears organization, over decades as a player, coach, and proud icon and ambassador for our organization, is immeasurable," the statement said. "His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level, but also created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations."

As for the current Bears, they will take the field for Sunday's game against the Packers with a 3-1 record on the season and a two-game winning streak in the rivalry.

Chicago defeated Green Bay in Week 16 of the 2025 campaign and then eliminated the Packers in the NFC Wild Card Round of the playoffs.

articles.title: Bears to honor legendary coach Mike Ditka with No. 89 helmet decal
articles.summary: The Bears will continue to honor Mike Ditka.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears continued to honor legendary head coach Mike Ditka in Week 5. Ditka, who led the Bears to a win in Super Bowl XX, died Friday. He was 86 .

In tribute to Ditka, the team unveiled a helmet decal featuring No. 89, the number Ditka wore when he was a tight end with the franchise. The Bears retired the number in 2013, and team chairman George McCaskey said it will be the last number the Bears retire.

The decal will appear on the back of the team's helmet, just under the American flag.

While Ditka is arguably more known for his stint as a head coach, he began his legend as a tight end with the Bears. He is credited with redefining the position , becoming one of the first tight ends to be used as a major receiving threat.

In his six seasons with the Bears, Ditka made five Pro Bowls and was a two-time first-team All-Pro selection. He gained 4,503 receiving yards and scored 34 touchdowns with the franchise. Ditka later played for the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys.

His excellence as a player got him inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame while he was still coaching.

As a coach, Ditka excelled with the Bears. In 11 seasons with the franchise, he posted a .631 winning percentage and won a Super Bowl. Following his time in Chicago, Ditka coached the New Orleans Saints, where he went 15-33 in three seasons.

His excellence as a player and coach, combined with his outspoken personality, made Ditka a popular figure in the game, even after his retirement. Because of that, multiple people and organizations paid tribute to Ditka on Friday.

The Bears will added one more tribute to that list Sunday.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Draws Concern from Doctors Ahead of Return from Injury, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will play Sunday's game against the New York Giants, but there is reportedly concern from the medical community that he will likely re-injure his left elbow.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will play Sunday's game against the New York Giants, but there is reportedly concern from the medical community that he will likely re-injure his left elbow.

"There are doctors around the NFL who believe it's a matter of when, not if, Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels hurts his left elbow again," ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday.

Schefter noted that Daniels received an "overwhelming opinion was that playing with a brace was a viable option" when visiting with specialists.

However, "there are doctors around the league who, despite not having examined Daniels, maintain that a player who dislocates his elbow twice—as Daniels has over the past 11 months—is at a higher risk suffering another dislocation."

He was still in good spirits before his expected return against the Giants, warming up with basketball shots in the rain:

Daniels suffered a dislocated elbow during Washington's 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sept. 20.

On Monday, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told reporters that the team expected Daniels to return in Week 5.

He was listed as a limited participant in Washington's three days of practice leading up to a Week 4 clash with the Indianapolis Colts, but was ultimately ruled out of the contest.

Daniels earned a Pro Bowl nod to go along with Offensive Rookie of the Year honors during his 2024 campaign, helping lead the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game.

He was limited to just seven contests in 2025 due to an elbow dislocation as Washington posted a 5-12 record, though.

In Daniels' first two games this year, he completed 56.9 percent of his passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns without tossing an interception. He also rushed for 100 yards on just 12 attempts.

Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis will be his backup for Sunday's game because Marcus Mariota is out with a sprained MCL.

Washington currently owns a 1-3 record, sitting at No. 4 in the NFC East standings.

articles.title: 'Uber-Talented' Drew Mestemaker Eyed for 2027 NFL Draft by Insider Despite 2028 Buzz
articles.summary: Drew Mestemaker may not have been on the top of many draft boards coming into the 2027 season, but the Oklahoma State quarterback is turning heads through five games.
articles.body:
Drew Mestemaker may not have been on the top of many draft boards coming into the 2027 season, but the Oklahoma State quarterback is turning heads through five games.

Nick Baumgardner of The Athletic called Mestemaker an "uber-talented" prospect who "is a confident downfield passer with enough athleticism to be a real problem at the next level."

Baumgardner's colleague, Dane Brugler, said he is "buying all the stock I can, regardless of whether he becomes a 2027 or '28 prospect," which is notable. After all, Baumgardner added that the signal-caller "ultimately could be a 2028 prospect" even though "it's impossible to watch him and not see first-round stuff."

The 2027 quarterback class is a crowded one with a number of players who could eventually garner first-round consideration in the pre-draft process.

Last month, B/R's NFL Scouting Department released a big board of prospects and ranked Mestemaker as the seventh-best quarterback behind Miami's Darian Mensah, Oregon's Dante Moore, Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss, Texas' Arch Manning, Notre Dame's CJ Carr and USC's Jayden Maiava.

That is a number of high-profile prospects at the position, and it doesn't even include Ohio State's Julian Sayin and Missouri's Austin Simmons. They have each received first-round consideration to this point as well and will have opportunities to play their way up big boards as the season progresses.

But even in a crowded group of quarterbacks, Mestemaker has stood out for the Cowboys.

He has completed 67.5 percent of his passes for 1,575 yards, 13 touchdowns and five interceptions while adding two more scores on the ground as a runner. He has thrown for more than 300 yards in each of his last four games, including in Oklahoma State's notable win over Oregon.

Mestemaker showed off his ability to impact the game in multiple ways against the Ducks when he threw for 317 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while also running for 109 yards and a score.

If he continues to play at such a level as Oklahoma State competes in the Big 12, he figures to remain a factor in 2027 NFL draft discussions.

articles.title: Crackers start in London as first kickoff return touchdown of NFL season nullified and two players ejected
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars' 90-yard kickoff return touchdown was nullified by multiple flags, and two linebackers were ejected on the opening play.
articles.body: If the point of playing games in London is to give the Brits a taste of, as they say over there, crackers NFL action then Sunday's game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium did that from the start. On the opening kickoff of this game ... Eagles kicker Jake Elliott kicked the ball 55 yards to the Jacksonville 10-yard line and Josh Cameron returned it 90 yards for a touchdown. It marked the first kickoff return touchdown in the NFL this season. NFL EXECS AND COACHES WANT LEAGUE TO REIN IN 'OUT OF CONTROL' OFFICIALS AND HOPE SUSPENSIONS SIGNAL A START But, no! Back upfield, officials – they had quite a week, by the way – had thrown multiple flags on the play. Two of those officials saw so much hijinks they threw their flag and then, seeing a second foul, threw their caps. NFL REFEREES JEFF SEEMAN AND ADRIAN HILL SUSPENDED AFTER UNPROFESSIONAL CLASHES WITH PLAYERS IN WEEK 4 So, with bated breath, we waited for the official announcement. And we learned both teams were flagged on the kickoff and players from both teams were flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct. The touchdown was thus nullified because the Eagles lined up in an illegal formation and the Jaguars had linebacker Branson Combs called for holding. Nice start to a game. Then we learned that Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jacksonville linebacker Bryan Thomas Jr. were both flagged for giving each other the business. It seems both men engaged in a block during the play and carried their standoff all the way to midfield where Trotter slammed Thomas to the turf after the play was over and then Thomas kicked up at Trotter while on his back. Both were flagged. Both were disqualified for the rest of the game – on a play that didn't even count. That hurt the Eagles more as Trotter was expected to get work with the starting defense while Thomas is exclusively a special teams contributor. So to recap: A season-first kickoff return touchdown was nullified by a penalty while a player from either team was ejected. It took officials a couple of minutes to sort it all. This game was bonkers from the beginning and then the crowd, a majority of which are Eagles fans, saw something perhaps stranger: The Eagles attempted to convert a fourth-and-1 play on their first possession but did not employ the Tush Push. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The team that turned the play into a major NFL play lined up in shotgun and ran the ball. The conversion attempt failed. So why? Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been nursing a calf injury recently, and the Eagles offensive line is something of a work in progress. The Eagles are without starting center Drew Kendall this game as they traded left guard Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens last week, and right tackle Lane Johnson retired. And all that begs the question: Why did Eagles coach Nick Sirianni go for it on fourth-and-1 in the first place? FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Status for Vikings vs. Saints Announced After Signing New Contract
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. will not make his Minnesota Vikings debut on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints and was officially inactive.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. will not make his Minnesota Vikings debut on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints and was officially inactive .

The Vikings elevated Beckham from the practice squad to the active roster before their road game, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

However, the team determined to keep him out despite an injury to Jordan Addision. Justin Jefferson will at least be healthy for Minnesota:

Minnesota signed Beckham to its practice squad on Wednesday, eight days after the New York Giants released the veteran.

Beckham largely dominated the NFL during his first stint with the Giants (2014-2018). He made three Pro Bowls and two All-Pro Second Teams and posted 1,000+ yards in every season except 2017, which ended early due to a fractured left ankle.

The Giants traded Beckham to the Cleveland Browns in 2019. He had another 1,000-yard season but suffered a torn ACL in 2020, ending his season after seven games. Beckham has dealt with numerous injuries since then and has enjoyed only one close-to-full season (2023, with the Baltimore Ravens) this decade.

Beckham showed the Giants enough to make the 53-man roster coming out of training camp.

It didn't work out in New York. Head coach John Harbaugh's team relies heavily on tight ends and has consistently used only three wideouts—Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields, and Darnell Mooney. Beckham saw only one catchless target in limited action with the Giants over three games.

articles.title: Caleb Williams Injury Update, Latest Return Timeline for Bears QB
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is inactive for Week 5 against the Green Bay Packers but has a chance to return in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is inactive for Week 5 against the Green Bay Packers but has a chance to return in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that Williams "could return sometime in the next several weeks."

Williams practiced Friday on a limited basis and Bears head coach Ben Johnson addresses his recovery:

Still, Pelissero suggested Chicago is willing to be patient with his recovery. The NFL insider cited the Bears' next two games (Oct. 18 against the Falcons and Oct. 22 against the New England Patriots) as possible occasions for him to be activated.

They'll have a long turnaround between Weeks 7 and 8, 11 days, which would afford Williams more time to recuperate and sharpen up if he needs it.

The third-year signal-caller began his 2026 season with an explosive performance during a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 269 yards and two touchdowns while adding 65 rushing yards and two more scores.

Unfortunately, Williams suffered a Grade 2 right hamstring strain while he was running for the end zone in the fourth quarter of the Bears' Week 2 game against the Minnesota Vikings (9-3 loss). Williams fell to the ground on the six-yard line on a non-contact play and was stretchered off the field.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Sept. 27 that the injury could sideline him for "three-to-four weeks."

The Bears selected Williams, a former Oklahoma and USC star, with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft. He and the Bears broke out in 2025, the first season under head coach Ben Johnson. Chicago won the NFC North and reached the NFC Divisional round thanks in part due to Williams' late-game heroics. He ended up throwing for 3,942 passing yards and 27 touchdowns.

Without Williams, Tyson Bagent is the team's interim starter, and Case Keenum is the backup.

Keenum starred in Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles in a 27-7 win after Bagent missed most of practice leading to the game ( concussion protocol ). He finished with 247 passing yards and two touchdowns. Bagent took over the following week and led the Bears to a 23-12 win (268 passing yards).

articles.title: Will Shipley Injured, Latest on Eagles RB & Dameon Pierce Fantasy Outlook with Saquon Barkley Out
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles confirmed running back Will Shipley won't return to Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars after suffering a foot injury.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles confirmed running back Will Shipley won't return to Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars after suffering a foot injury.

Shipley scored Philly's first touchdown in the second quarter before exiting.

His absence leaves Dameon Pierce as the No. 1 option on the ground with Saquon Barkley sidelined because of a hamstring issue.

From a fantasy football perspective, the fifth-year ball-carrier is unlikely to emerge as a must-add on the waiver wire after Week 5. Following an encouraging rookie season in 2022, he has combined to run for 745 yards and four touchdowns in 30 appearances.

The Eagles only promoted Pierce to the active roster earlier this week. He signed to the practice squad in September after failing to make the final August cut.

Somebody obviously has to carry the ball for Philadelphia, and the list of internal options is getting thin. Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve, and it's too early to forecast the statuses of Shipley and Barkley in Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers.

Maybe Pierce gets the nod against Carolina. He showed little with the Houston Texans and Kansas City Chiefs in the previous three years, though, and the state of Philly's offensive line does him and every other running back few favors.

The Eagles traded guard/center Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens and watched Lane Johnson retire. Another multi-time Pro Bowler, Landon Dickerson, is on IR.

Fantasy managers would be advised to wait and see how the backfield evolves before considering any accompany moves.

articles.title: 'Major Sickness Running Through' Saints' Locker Room Ahead of Vikings Game, New Report Reveals
articles.summary: The health of the New Orleans Saints reportedly could be a significant factor during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
The health of the New Orleans Saints reportedly could be a significant factor during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.

Insider Nick Underhill reported "there's a major sickness running through the locker room" ahead of the contest. The report came less than two hours before the 1 p.m. ET kickoff time with New Orleans preparing for the game.

The Saints announced their list of inactives for the matchup, and it included six players and Zach Wilson listed as the third quarterback. Edge-rusher Anfernee Jennings, safety Mike Reid, linebacker Kaden Elliss, offensive guard Jeremiah Wright, and defensive linemen Vernon Broughton and Nathan Sheperd were all ruled out.

It should be noted none of them were listed with an illness in the injury report leading up to the game.

Instead, New Orleans' Friday injury report listed just defensive tackle Christen Miller as questionable because of "illness."

Miller was not on the team's inactives in the Sunday announcement.

The Saints are looking to get back on track following three straight losses, the most recent of which came in blowout fashion on Monday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons.

Offense hasn't been an issue with at least 24 points in each of the team's four games, but the defense is last in the league in points allowed per game (32.0).

Dealing with an undefeated Vikings team while also battling illness throughout the locker room likely won't make life much easier for the Saints even if they are at home for Sunday's game.

articles.title: Jason Kelce’s Eagles-Jaguars broadcast shows why NFL booths could use more offensive linemen
articles.summary: Jason Kelce's high school long-snapping experience made DaVon Hamilton's emergency role one of the best moments of the Eagles-Jaguars broadcast.
articles.body: Jason Kelce made an emergency long snapper one of the most interesting parts of Eagles-Jaguars on Sunday morning. I wasn’t expecting to spend much time thinking about Jacksonville’s long-snapping situation when I turned on the game. But that’s where we ended up, and having a former offensive lineman in the booth made it worth listening to. Kelce joined Dave Pasch and Kurt Warner for NFL Network’s broadcast from London. The assignment is one of four games on Kelce’s NFL Network schedule this season. The combination worked really well. Warner can explain the game from the quarterback’s perspective, while Kelce spent his career dealing with everything happening directly in front of the quarterback. CRACKERS START IN LONDON AS FIRST KICKOFF RETURN TOUCHDOWN OF NFL SEASON NULLIFIED AND TWO PLAYERS EJECTED Most game broadcasts spend a lot of time talking about quarterback play, and rightfully so: it's the most important position on the field. That said, it was refreshing to get some perspective from a former offensive lineman and it added depth to the presentation. Jason Kelce knows long snapping After Jaguars long snapper Ross Matiscik suffered a shoulder injury, Jacksonville turned to defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton. Long snapper isn't a position most fans spend much time thinking about (at least not until something goes horribly wrong), but it's a critical position. Kelce had actually done the job in high school and knew something about the difficulty of doing it as a very large human being. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "When I got fat, when I put on weight, I used to long-snap in high school," Kelce said. "When I got to over 300 pounds-ish, it became really hard to look in between your legs." Well, there’s something I hadn’t considered. Hamilton, a 29-year-old, 6-foot-4, 335-pound defensive tackle who long snapped in high school, was being asked to handle a job that could swing the game with one bad snap. Kelce was enjoying Hamilton’s effort, too. "Way to go, DaVon Hamilton. I love it." ESPN STAR STEPHEN A. SMITH'S LANE JOHNSON, EAGLES RANT TRIGGERS IMMEDIATE VIDEO APOLOGY Warner, meanwhile, wanted to correct Kelce’s description of himself. "You’ve never been fat. You’re just husky." Some viewers have already had enough of Jason Kelce The reviews on X were considerably less friendly in places. "Jason Kelce is on the call for Jaguars/Eagles?… Yeah, this won’t be a biased broadcast at all," one user wrote. Another viewer said: "Yeah I’m sorry, Jason Kelce cannot do Eagles games. Clear bias and won’t stop talking." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Playing for the Eagles doesn’t automatically make Kelce a bad choice to call their games. Judge him on what he says. Kelce did lay it on a little thick when praising Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni for calling a timeout late in the first half. The timeout gave replay officials more time to look at a potential fumble. It was a smart move, but Kelce was a little over-the-top in his approval. The other main complaint was that Kelce talked too much. One user posted, "Jason Kelce hasn’t stopped talking," while another viewer accused him of leaving Warner with nothing to do. I don't agree with that assessment. The three-man booth can be challenging to navigate and often one analyst spends more time talking. But I felt the distribution made sense. There’s room for Kelce’s enthusiasm alongside Warner’s analysis, especially when they’re looking at the game from different positions. The long-snapping sequence was my favorite part, but I’d like to hear that quarterback-center conversation on more broadcasts. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD And social media wasn't entirely negative. Chase Senior had a take I agreed with: "I actually think this role suits him better than being on the set for ESPN." Kelce is a natural as a game broadcaster. I wouldn’t be surprised if a network offers him a nice raise to do it full-time.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ plans for life after football are becoming clearer as his final season reveals what matters most to him
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has called 2026 his final season, and what comes after is starting to come into focus.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has called 2026 his final season, and what comes after is starting to come into focus. On SiriusXM's Mad Dog Sports Radio, the Steelers quarterback was asked where he sees himself in 12 months. His reported answer was that he would be tending to his pregnant wife. Rodgers has not formally announced a pregnancy, and he has kept his wife Brittani out of public view. Even so, the comment fits a pattern that has been building for months. A 42-year-old quarterback is making room for a very different life.What do Aaron Rodgers' plans for life after football look like?Aaron Rodgers has framed this season as the end of a 22-year career, and he has been direct about it. He has said there is "zero debate" about retiring, which shuts down the usual guessing game. The private side is a different matter. He confirmed he married in 2025, said he first met his wife in 2017, and has explained that she has no social media and wants to stay out of the spotlight. Her identity, he has said, will come out only if she decides it should.That restraint stands out. Rodgers is not shy on podcasts and radio, yet this is the one topic he protects.As reported, his answer to a year-out question had no team, no studio job and no business deal in it. It was about home. If the pregnancy report is accurate, his first year after football would be built around a newborn, not a new career.How has family changed Aaron Rodgers heading into his last season?The clearest example came this summer. Rodgers ended a long estrangement from his family, and he credited his wife for making it possible. "She is the big impetus behind that," he told The Athletic, though he was careful to say she never pushed him. It was her love and support, he explained, that let him open up to the idea.It took a couple of years of talking and spending time together. He called getting those relationships back a real blessing.The 2017 meeting also adds some context. Rodgers said on The Pat McAfee Show in March that he knew early he wanted to be with her. The wedding came in 2025, and he was spotted with a ring in June of that year, before he confirmed the marriage. More than a year later, he is still guarding the details.Pittsburgh opened its season against the Falcons on Sept. 13, and Rodgers has played with an end date in sight. That changes how his comments read. Family talk is no longer a side note to a football story. It looks like the plan.For now, the pregnancy remark is a hint, not a confirmation. articles.title: New Cowboys Rumors on 'Trust' in DC Christian Parker amid Struggles Compared to Matt Eberflus
articles.summary: Despite the Dallas Cowboys' early-season struggles defensively, the team reportedly still feels good about defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
articles.body:
Despite the Dallas Cowboys' early-season struggles defensively, the team reportedly still feels good about defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

Appearing on Fox NFL Sunday , Fox Sports NFL insider Jay Glazer said the Cowboys "believe" in Parker unlike Matt Eberflus, who was the defensive coordinator last season:

Glazer said players didn't trust or like Eberflus' scheme last season, but they do like Parker's scheme and believe they will "mesh and jell" as the season goes on.

Through their first five games of the 2026 campaign, the Cowboys rank 31st in the NFL in total defense and 26th in scoring defense, allowing 27.2 points per game.

After giving up 30 or more points in three consecutive games, the Cowboys held the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to 24 on Thursday night, but they still lost the game 24-16 to fall to 2-3 on the year.

Tampa started an undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels and still managed to rack up 419 yards of total offense on Dallas' defense.

Much of the damage was done on the ground, as the Bucs rushed for 241 yards, led by Bucky Irving with 165 yards.

The Cowboys' defensive shortcomings are nothing new, as they ranked 28th in total defense and 31st in scoring defense in 2024, and 30th in total defense and 32nd in scoring defense last season.

Parker is the Cowboys' fourth different defensive coordinator in the past four seasons, so a lack of continuity could have something to do with the issues on that side of the ball.

The 34-year-old Parker was a highly touted coaching candidate this past offseason after serving as the Philadelphia Eagles' passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach in 2024 and 2025.

He helped the Eagles win a Super Bowl in 2024 and coached up defensive backs Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean to the point that they were both First Team All-Pro selections last season.

After acquiring talented cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers last week, the Cowboys front office may be hopeful that Parker can work some similar magic with him.

articles.title: Jaguars Stun Eagles on Late FG, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Hurts, Lawrence, Washington, More
articles.summary: Sunday's game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles in London was, in a word, chaos.
articles.body:
Sunday's game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles in London was, in a word, chaos.

And that chaos ended with Cam Little hitting the game-winning 57-yard field goal for the Jaguars just seconds after Jake Elliott gave the Eagles the lead with a 48-yard field goal.

Ameer Abdullah's 53-yard kick return before Little's field goal was arguably the most important play of the game in Jacksonville's 19-17 win, and defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton also deserves some credit for filling in at long-snapper and delivering the snap on the last kick.

Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars are now 4-1 following their third straight win, while Jalen Hurts and the shorthanded Eagles who were without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith fell to 2-3 overall with a third straight loss.

To say Philadelphia entered this game reeling would be an understatement.

In addition to the two straight losses, they were without key players in Barkley, Smith, Jonathan Greenard and Tank Bigsby, among others, because of injury. What's more, the offensive line looked completely different after Lane Johnson retired and Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens.

And it took exactly one play for the NFC East team to lose another key contributor.

The game fittingly started with chaos, as Jacksonville's Josh Cameron returned the opening kickoff for a touchdown before it was called back for holding. A fight broke out, which resulted in the ejections of Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. (not wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.).

Philadelphia then turned it over on downs on its first offensive possession before Parker Washington scored a 51-yard touchdown on the ensuing drive for Jacksonville. There was a sense of here we go again for the Eagles, but they responded in a major way.

Will Shipley's touchdown and Darius Cooper's 62-yard score gave them the lead, and the defense protected it with a goal-line stand to end the first half with a 14-7 advantage. Jalen Carter in particular was unblockable, which shut down Lawrence and Co. for extended stretches.

Perhaps there was some hesitancy from Jacksonville's perspective to kick a field goal at the end of the half since Hamilton was playing long snapper.

But the Eagles still faced an uphill battle after halftime even with the lead, as Shipley was ruled out with a foot injury. The running game was virtually nonexistent as both offenses stalled with a Philadelphia turnover on downs and a Quinyon Mitchell interception of Lawrence during an ugly third quarter that featured three combined points.

The game got uglier from there with Hurts missing a wide-open Dontayvion Wicks for a touchdown and the Jaguars offense turning into a comedy show from the Eagles' 1-yard line with a false start, two delay of games, Brian Thomas Jr. not getting a second foot down in the end zone and Lawrence throwing an incompletion on fourth down.

But that offense finally broke through when Washington made a highlight-reel one-handed touchdown catch. While Jacksonville missed the ensuing extra point after a poor snap from Hamilton, it finally had the lead.

That lead didn't last long thanks to Elliott's field goal, but Little had a response as time expired for a Jaguars team that will remain in London to face the Houston Texans.

articles.title: Will Lamar Jackson play in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons tonight? Latest injury update on the Baltimore Ravens quarterback
articles.summary: It’s hard to imagine Lamar Jackson going through a new season without an injury. Many now take it for granted that he will get hurt and miss time.
articles.body: It’s hard to imagine Lamar Jackson going through a new season without an injury.Many now take it for granted that he will get hurt and miss time. This inevitably becomes the narrative for why he falls short in the regular season - or, if he does finish it, why he fails to advance deep into the playoffs toward the Super Bowl.This recalls First Things First host Nick Wright’s comments on the Baltimore Ravens quarterback: “Being damn near 30 and not figuring out how not to get sick every winter when your job demands you be at your best every winter? Speaks to immaturity.”Is Lamar Jackson playing against the Atlanta Falcons?No, Lamar Jackson won’t play in the Week 5 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter announced Friday that Tyler Hunley would start at Atlanta.Jackson missed practice all week with a left ankle injury he suffered during the Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans. He did not practice all week. He was ruled out for the Week 5 game vs. Falcons.Tyler Huntley filled in for Jackson in the second half and completed 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards, leading Baltimore to victory over Tennessee.“We have a ton of confidence in [Huntley] to play really well,” head coach Jesse Minter said. “I think everyone on the team is excited to see that.”Lamar Jackson injury riskAs per Draft Sharks, Lamar Jackson has a medium injury risk. His durability score is 5, the highest possible being 5.Nick Wright’s comments on Lamar JacksonFOX Sports host Nick Wright criticized Lamar Jackson for repeatedly missing practice during the winter season due to illness. Wright said that Jackson has continued the “missing trend” for six consecutive years. The host also questioned the Baltimore Ravens quarterback’s week-to-week health status.“He’s the only franchise quarterback in this league that we expect every winter to get sick and have it show up on an injury report,” Wright said in Dec. 2025.“It’s been six winters in a row that this has happened. And the only one that it didn’t was when he missed winter with an injury. He’s the only franchise quarterback in this league that the team seems to have no line on his Week-to-Week, Day-to-Day health status.”Wright described Jackson’s demeanor on social media and his response to adversity as signs of immaturity. The host argued that Jackson should have taken responsibility for managing his health and availability, as a professional athlete approaching 30 years of age and a franchise quarterback.“Within the game? Doesn’t face much adversity. But when he does, I think we see some immaturity. The way he uses social media? Speaks to immaturity.Being damn near 30 and not figuring out how not to get sick every winter when your job demands you be at your best every winter? Speaks to immaturity,” Wright said.“He’s the most important person in this franchise. He’s an adult. He’s a professional athlete. And he’s the only, forget star, just starting quarterback in this league that every single year, he can’t manage to figure out how not to get the seasonal flu and miss practice. articles.title: NFL London: Last-second Cam Little kick means Jacksonville Jaguars beat Philadelphia Eagles
articles.summary: Cam Little kicks a 57-yard field goal in the final second to seal a 19-17 victory for the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Philadelphia Eagles in an exhilarating NFL London game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
articles.body:
Cam Little kicked a 57-yard field goal in the final second to seal a 19-17 victory for the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Philadelphia Eagles in an exhilarating NFL London game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The Jaguars had conceded the lead with eight seconds remaining after the Eagles completed their own 48-yard field goal, but Ameer Abdullah made 53 yards on the return before being tackled with a second on the clock.

The 23-year-old Little completed the lengthy pressure kick and tore off his helmet, racing to the end of the pitch to celebrate in front of the fans, arms outstretched, before being mobbed by his team-mates.

The game featured drama in its opening moments as Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr and Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr were ejected for fighting on the opening kick-off.

Josh Cameron had scored a 90-yard touchdown for the Jaguars from the kick-off, but the score was nullified for the penalties resulting from Trotter seemingly shoving his opponent to the ground before appearing to receive a kick in return.

The Eagles, who were missing their top two running backs in Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby, were the first to concede when Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington reached the endzone in the first quarter.

In perhaps a nod to Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney, Washington did a boxing knockout celebration.

However, the Eagles went into half-time with a 14-3 lead following touchdowns from third-choice running back Will Shipley and wide receiver Darius Cooper.

Little's 34-yard field goal cut the deficit in the third quarter, although he missed the extra-point kick when Parker Washington's 27-yard touchdown gave the Jaguars a 16-14 lead with three minutes and 20 seconds remaining.

This time, Washington copied Chelsea forward Cole Palmer's cold celebration.

Jake Elliott appeared to have completed a winning kick in the closing moments, before the Jaguars' special-teams line-up set up Little for a dramatic conclusion.

The Jaguars are now on a three-match winning streak, while the Eagles are on a losing run of the same length.

The Florida franchise sit top of AFC South early in round five with a 4-1 record, while the Eagles are second in NFC South with both their wins coming in their opening two fixtures.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni Takes Blame for Eagles Loss to Jaguars, Explains Kickoff Decision Before GW FG
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles saw their comeback win against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday slip away in a matter of seconds, and head coach Nick Sirianni took the blame.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles saw their comeback win against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday slip away in a matter of seconds, and head coach Nick Sirianni took the blame.

"I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game," he told reporters. "And that's what I said to our guys. What hurts there is that the guys fought so hard and I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game. … I put that fully on me."

It seemed as if Philadelphia was going to win when Jalen Hurts moved the offense into field-goal range on its final offensive possession. Jake Elliott drilled the go-ahead 48-yarder with just eight seconds remaining, which figured to be enough to escape London with a win.

And then the Eagles decided to kick the ball off in bounds.

Ameer Abdullah made them pay with a 53-yard return, which set up Cam Little's 57-yard field goal as time expired.

For his part, Elliott confirmed after the game he was told to kick the ball in bounds:

Jacksonville didn't have a timeout remaining, so booting the ball into the end zone or even out of bounds would have left the offense with perhaps one more play to come away with a miracle touchdown.

Instead, Abdullah had time to return the kick into Philadelphia territory and set the Jaguars up for a dramatic victory.

It was a stunning defeat for the Eagles, who have now lost three in a row. Sirianni will face plenty of questions after the way the end of the game unfolded, although he took full responsibility in the aftermath of the latest defeat.

articles.title: NFL in London: Cam Little kicks game-winning field goal as Jacksonville Jaguars beat Philadelphia Eagles 19-17 in Tottenham Hotspur Stadium thriller
articles.summary: Cam Little kicks 57-yard field goal as time expires to give Jacksonville win over Philadelphia; Eagles kicker Jake Elliott had hit 48-yarder for lead with 12 seconds remaining; game had a record Tottenham Hotspur NFL attendance of 61,322
articles.body:
Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw a 27-yard touchdown to Parker Washington on fourth down with under four minutes remaining to give them a 16-14 lead, and when they forced the Eagles to punt with two minutes left, the win looked all but secure.

But when Jalen Hurts led the Eagles 32 yards downfield in nine plays to set up a Jake Elliott 48-yard field goal with 12 seconds to go, the Eagles-heavy crowd celebrated what appeared to be a 17-16 Philadelphia win in London.

However, those 12 seconds were enough for Ameer Abdullah to stun the stadium with a 53-yard kick-off return, before Little hit the game-winner as time expired.

The Jags move to 4-1 on the season and look every part the Super Bowl contender after a supreme performance from Lawrence.

Meanwhile, after a turbulent season so far filled with injuries and disappointment, the Eagles fall to 2-3.

The game started in as chaotic a fashion as it ended. Jacksonville's Josh Cameron took the kick-off back 90 yards for a touchdown, only for flags, hats and fists to fly. The play was nullified, players from both teams were ejected and the game restarted.

The Jags opened the scoring shortly afterwards. Lawrence rolled out to his right and hit Washington in stride, with the receiver racing down the sideline and cutting back for a 51-yard score.

The Eagles struck back twice to take the lead, with Will Shipley's two-yard score followed by a 61-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper where, reminiscent of Washington's touchdown for the Jags, he beat defenders and raced to the end zone.

There was more drama before the half, as the Jags drove 68 yards in a 17-play drive, only to be stopped four times from the Eagles' one-yard line and leave the score at 14-7.

Little added three points in the third quarter but both teams fully took hold of the game. Quinyon Mitchell intercepted Lawrence, while Hurts missed a wide-open Dontayvion Wicks as the Jags sent all-out pressure on a third down.

The Eagles stopped the Jags again at the goal line, as the Philadelphia-heavy crowd forced a turnover on downs after a pair of delay-of-game flags, but when Lawrence had another chance to put together a drive, he did not waste it.

He dropped the ball right into the arms of a diving Washington for an incredible score.

After that, the pair of exchanged field goals provided a fitting ending to one of the great NFL games in London.

articles.title: Parker Washington is earning himself a major payday on next deal
articles.summary: Parker Washington’s breakout start to 2026 is strengthening his case for a major payday as he approaches free agency
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars narrowly defeated the Philadelphia Eagles , 19-17, in a Week 5 game from London, and once again, it was another big day from Parker Washington.

With this performance -- and in his overall play this season -- Washington is making it clear that the Jaguars can't afford to let him walk away.

Washington delivered his biggest performance of the season Sunday in London, catching six passes for 124 yards and two touchdowns in Jacksonville's 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

His first touchdown came on a 51-yard catch-and-run that gave the Jaguars an early lead. His second was considerably more dramatic: a one-handed 27-yard touchdown grab in the fourth quarter that put the Jaguars back in front with just over three minutes remaining.

It was another reminder of just how far Washington has come since being selected in the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft.

Washington entered the final year of his rookie contract this season after breaking out in 2025, when he led the Jaguars with 847 receiving yards on 58 receptions and scored five touchdowns. He is currently scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent in March, as he and Jacksonville have so far been unable to come to terms.

And this season, his play has only strengthened his negotiating position.

Through five games, Washington has 22 receptions for 352 yards and four touchdowns. His quiet seven-yard performance against Cincinnati in Week 4 now looks considerably more like an outlier than a sign of a diminished role.

Sunday also showed the different ways Washington can affect a game.

The 51-yard touchdown showcased his ability to create an explosive play after the catch. The fourth-quarter score showed Washington making a difficult one-handed grab in a high-leverage situation with Jacksonville trailing. It is the kind of versatility that has made Washington one of Trevor Lawrence's most trusted targets.

Before the season, Washington said he wasn't focused on his contract situation and would leave those discussions to his agent. His job, he said, was simply to continue making plays for Lawrence. And so far, that approach appears to be working.

The longer Washington continues producing at this level, the more expensive keeping him in Jacksonville is likely to become. And after Sunday's performance in London, Washington has given the Jaguars another compelling reason to make sure somebody else isn't the team writing that check.

articles.title: "It's Not a Stigma": Russell Wilson & Bill Cowher Take Strong Stand on Mental Health After Eagles Legend's Retirement
articles.summary: For years, NFL players have been expected to push through pain and keep going. But Lane Johnson’s decision to step away from football has brought attention t...
articles.body:
For years, NFL players have been expected to push through pain and keep going. But Lane Johnson's decision to step away from football has brought attention to a different struggle, one that can be harder to recognize and discuss openly: mental health.

Bill Cowher and Russell Wilson addressed that issue on NFL on CBS Sports as they reacted to Johnson's retirement. Both backed the Philadelphia Eagles legend's decision and stressed that seeking help should never be something an athlete feels ashamed of.

"I applaud his transparency; Good for him for doing so because so many times we put a stigma on that. It's not a stigma to talk about trying to deal with mental health," Cowher said on Sunday . "There are clinicians in every NFL building that you go into, so seeking that is not a problem."

"I think the better you are, the harder it is to walk away," Cowher said.

The Pro Football Hall of Fame coach also pointed to how difficult it can be for an elite player to know when to walk away. Cowher turned to Wilson, his colleague on the CBS pregame show, and asked about his own experience of weighing what comes next after years in the NFL.

Wilson understood the challenge. After spending 14 seasons in the NFL, the Super Bowl-winning quarterback knows what it means to build a career around football and then face questions about the next stage of life.

"It's the hardest decision in life when you've been on the mountaintop for a long period of time," Wilson said. "And I think Lane has been on the mountaintop as an all-time pro at his position, but also in the National Football League, winning Super Bowls."

Wilson also stressed that family and loved ones should remain central to such a decision. He said Johnson had made the right choice for himself and highlighted the need to think about mental wellness, not just mental health.

"The mental health thing is so important. I always think about mental wellness, too. It's not just about mental health. It already sounds like we're already sick. I think about mental wellness and how make sure we do things well," Wilson said.

Johnson announced his retirement on October 6 after 14 seasons, all with Philadelphia. The 36-year-old had hoped to play one more year, but said his personal and family priorities had changed.

"Right now, it is critical that I focus on my mental health," Johnson wrote in his retirement statement.

His decision drew widespread support from former teammates and people around the league, but it also sparked controversy. ESPN personality Stephen A. Smith questioned the timing of Johnson's retirement on First Take, making comments that were widely criticized for appearing to trivialize the mental health concerns Johnson had cited.

Smith later apologized on the show, admitting that he was wrong and had made light of the issue. He said he had intended to criticize the Eagles' situation, not Johnson's decision, but acknowledged that his remarks had not made that distinction clear.

Cowher and Wilson also made it clear that athletes should not have to justify seeking help. Players should be able to speak openly about their struggles without facing criticism for putting their health first.

Johnson retires with an impressive resume. He won two Super Bowls with Philadelphia, made six Pro Bowls, and earned two first-team All-Pro selections. He has also spoken publicly about his mental health struggles, using his own experiences to raise awareness.

Johnson's playing days are over, but the message from Cowher and Wilson applies well beyond football. After years of competing at the highest level, looking after one's health can be just as personal a decision as playing through the pain.

articles.title: Jaguars kicker sticks it to Eagles fans after nailing game-winning 57-yard field goal in London
articles.summary: Cam Little's 57-yard field goal stunned the Eagles after Ameer Abdullah's kickoff return set up the Jacksonville Jaguars for a dramatic finish.
articles.body: There’s nothing sweeter than an early-morning NFL game that goes down to the wire and leads you right into the afternoon kickoff. The Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles blessed us with that on Sunday. The game, while mostly sloppy from the start, saw the Jaguars and Eagles trade scores in the fourth quarter. Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington on fourth down to take the lead with 3:20 left in the game. Then, Eagles kicker Jake Elliott gave Philly a one-point lead with eight seconds left. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Philadelphia, for whatever reason, thought it was a good idea to boot the ball to a Jaguars returner instead of kicking it into the end zone and hoping Lawrence could chuck up a prayer to win the game. Ameer Abdullah broke away from Philadelphia’s special teams and got the ball across midfield and into Eagles territory with one second left. Jaguars kicker Cam Little nailed a game-winning 57-yard field goal. Jacksonville took home the 19-17 victory and moved to 4-1 on the season. Little immediately ran back toward the opposite end zone and taunted some of the Eagles fans who lined the barrier. Little’s kick probably would have been good from about 70 yards. His teammates lifted him up in celebration. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Eagles fell to 2-3 with the loss. The game was chaotic from the beginning. Jaguars rookie returner Josh Cameron thought he had a 90-yard kickoff return touchdown from the jump. It would have been the first kickoff-return TD in the NFL this year. Offsetting penalties nullified the return. On the same play, Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jaguars blocker Bryan Thomas Jr. got into a scuffle and were kicked out of the game. It certainly was a "crackers" start to the game, as OutKick’s Armando Salguero wrote this morning. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Despite having 13 penalties for 100 yards, Jacksonville was able to escape London with the dub.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni takes blame for Eagles' kickoff strategy in final minute: 'I cost us that game'
articles.summary: Nick Sirianni found himself in the crosshairs after a close loss.
articles.body:
After a hard-fought 59 minutes Sunday, it looked as though the Philadelphia Eagles had finally put the Jacksonville Jaguars away for good. Following a last-second field goal, all the Eagles needed to do was bury the Jaguars deep in their own territory and stop one more desperation play.

The Eagles, however, had other plans. With just 12 seconds left on the clock, the team decided to kick the ball to Jacksonville return man Ameer Abdullah. He made the Eagles pay, returning the kick 53 yards to put the Jaguars in field-goal range with just a second left on the clock.

The Jaguars took full advantage of the return, kicking a game-winning field goal as time expired to win the contest 19-17.

After the game, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni was asked about his team's strategy on that final kickoff. As some pointed out, the Eagles could have just kicked the ball out of bounds, giving the Jaguars the ball on their own 40-yard line and forcing the team to make a play or two before getting into field-goal range.

Sirianni admitted he made the decision to kick off normally and it cost his team the game. His full answer contained some NSFW language , but Sirianni eventually said he was the reason the Eagles lost the game.

"I didn't make the right decision and I lost us that game. And that's what I said to our guys. What hurts there is that the guys fought so hard, and then I don't make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game and I put that fully on me."

Jalen Hurts was also asked why the team didn't run out the clock more prior to the kick. He said that wasn't his place.

When asked about his thought process on that call, Sirianni declined to provide specifics.

Eagles kicker Jake Elliott was also asked about the play, and said he was told to kick it normally.

Kicking the ball out of bounds would not have guaranteed an Eagles win, but it would have put the Jaguars in an extremely tough situation. The team had zero timeouts remaining at the time of the kick, and would have needed to not only gain yards to get into field-goal position, but would have needed to find a way to stop the clock.

Knowing that, the Eagles' defense could have played close to the sideline to ensure any pass was properly covered. That would have left the middle of the field open, but a completion likely would have resulted in time running out before the Jaguars were able to spike the ball or get their kicking team out there for a possible game-winning kick.

The nature of the loss, and the kickoff decision by Sirianni, comes at an extremely rough time for the Eagles. The team entered Week 5 in a bit of a tailspin after losing to the Chicago Bears and Los Angeles Rams the previous two weeks.

On top of that, the Eagles were without No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith and star running back Saquon Barkley during the contest. Additionally, its offensive line was in shambles following the sudden retirement of Lane Johnson and the team trading away Cam Jurgens.

A win would have done a lot to curb all the negativity surrounding the team following its losing streak and recent loss of talent. Instead, the loss to the Jaguars in London only draws more attention to Sirianni's failures, something he can't afford after the team also disappointed fans last season.
